name: @dsh-external/project-nav
description: DSH plugin: anti-drift project governance — bidirectional feature<->file mapping, mainline vector, and a governance-first action ledger. v0.4.0: multi-session concurrency (per-scope leases + queueing) and scope file fingerprints. v0.5.0: architecture-first protocol (anchor gate, repeat-patch gate, nav_adr decision ledger). v0.6.0: convergence — architecture stays the core and everything else is auxiliary (10 tools, 5 data files). v0.7.0: every read-modify-write of shared state runs under a per-target file lock (index / docs / vector / ADR ledger / PROJECT.md), a lock whose owner died is broken by age, and the acquire loop waits asynchronously instead of blocking the event loop. v0.7.1: retirement semantics (nav_update retire=true) so a deleted feature/module/project can actually leave the index and cascade. v0.7.2: one resolver for scope files (indexedOwnersOf). v0.7.3: the repeat-patch gate counts patches — an action whose fingerprint proves it changed nothing is no longer counted, so bookkeeping passes stop manufacturing hollow ADRs. v0.7.4: two contract holes closed — the scope resolver no longer deletes project-prefixed index keys (fingerprinting had been silently off for 12 of 18 features, so drift went unreported), and a lapsed lease is no longer a dead end (the owner can re-begin, close out late or abort); plus read-side reconciliation (map/retire see the same truth as status), module re-homing, and a lock that breaks by rename + identity check instead of a racy unlink. v0.8.0 wires the architecture doc layer into the governance loop: every arch doc (.internal/arch/*.md with an arch-cache fingerprint header) becomes machine-tracked — nav_query prints an arch pointer line, nav_plan records archBasis and prints an architecture cross-check, nav_mark done reports which docs the change made stale, nav_status summarizes freshness, and the new nav_arch tool owns list/check/stamp. Rendering (SVG/HTML projection) stays outside the plugin; freshness compares instants rather than strings, so UTC, local-wall-clock and second-truncated stamp renderings all count as the same instant while real drift is still caught by size, a missing file or a later instant. v0.8.1 adds the workspace boundary: a session whose cwd belongs to a governed workspace is bound once at session start to the harness's native workspace-write sandbox, so write actions cannot leave that workspace while reads stay unrestricted everywhere. The plugin contributes only the one fact the harness cannot know — which workspaces this deployment governs — and never overrides a mode the user chose explicitly.
author: Fishsb (lk)
